libraries.name: ArduCAM Mini 2MP (OV2640)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A simulated Arducam Mini 2MP SPI camera (OV2640): it photographs the bench and gives real JPEG or RGB565 bytes from a 384 KB buffer, over the real module's SPI and I2C registers. Includes ArduCAM.h, so sketches for the real camera run. The view is rendered at 160 x 120 and scaled up to the chosen size. Not made by or affiliated with Arducam.

libraries.name: Bluetooth (HC-05)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The HC-05 Bluetooth serial module: whatever a phone sends comes out of its TXD as serial bytes, and whatever the board sends to its RXD goes to the phone. The phone is in the run panel: type a line and Send. Use SoftwareSerial or Serial1/Serial2.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: Buzzers and a microphone
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: An active buzzer (beeps by itself when powered), a passive buzzer (plays the note you give it with tone()) and a sound sensor (KY-038 microphone module) that hears what parts on the bench play. You hear the buzzers too: the toolbar's Sound button turns part sounds on and off (the microphone hears them either way).

libraries.name: Climate sensors
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Temperature and humidity: the DHT11 and DHT22 (one data wire) and the BME280 (I2C, with air pressure). Set the weather with sliders in the run panel. Includes DHT.h and Adafruit_BME280.h.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: Real-time clock (DS3231)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The DS3231 clock module: it keeps the date and time (starting from this PC's clock when the run starts, and running with the simulation: pausing pauses it) and has a thermometer. I2C at 0x68 (the same as an MPU-6050: they can't share a bus). Includes RTClib.h.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: Colour-tracking camera
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A small camera that finds the biggest patch of one colour (red, green, blue, yellow...) in what it sees and tells a board where it is over I2C, like the Pixy or HuskyLens cameras robots use. A screen on its back shows what it sees. Includes BlobCam.h for sketches.

libraries.name: Gear motor with encoder
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The yellow TT gear motor with a 20-slot encoder disc and an optical sensor on its shaft: its OUT pin changes as the slots pass, so a board can count how far and how fast it turned. Drive it like any TT motor (through a motor driver).

libraries.name: Gripper, fingerprint sensor, MP3 player, 7-segment digit
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A servo claw gripper that really grabs things, a fingerprint sensor (R307 / AS608, Adafruit_Fingerprint.h), the DFPlayer Mini MP3 player (DFRobotDFPlayerMini.h) and a single 7-segment LED digit.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: GPS module (NEO-6M)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A GPS receiver: after a few seconds it gets a fix and sends its position as NMEA sentences on its TX pin (9600 baud), once a second. Its position is where it is on the bench (the bench sits at a latitude and longitude you choose; north is -z): carry it about and the position follows. Includes TinyGPSPlus.h (and TinyGPS++.h).

libraries.name: IR remote and receiver
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The little 21-key infrared remote and an IR receiver module (VS1838B). Press the remote's keys in the run panel; every receiver on the bench picks up the code (NEC protocol). Includes IRremote.h, both its new (IrReceiver) and old (IRrecv) ways.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: Line, obstacle, laser and motion sensors
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Sensors robots use: the TCRT5000 line sensor (sees dark lines on a light floor), the FC-51 obstacle sensor (IR, a few cm), the VL53L0X laser distance sensor (I2C, up to 2 m) and the HC-SR501 PIR motion sensor. They really look at the bench. Includes VL53L0X.h and Adafruit_VL53L0X.h.

libraries.name: Joystick and rotary encoder
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A thumb joystick (KY-023: two knobs and a push button) and a rotary encoder knob (KY-040: clicks round in steps, and pushes). Work them from the run panel.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: Keypads
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Membrane keypads (4x4 and 4x3): each key joins its row wire to its column wire while it's held, exactly as the real ones do. Press the keys in the run panel. Includes Keypad.h.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: LCD 16x2 and 20x4 (I2C)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The classic blue 16x2 character LCD and its bigger 20x4 brother (HD44780) with an I2C backpack (PCF8574): text over just 2 wires. Includes LiquidCrystal_I2C.h for sketches; real firmware using LiquidCrystal_I2C works too.

libraries.name: LCD 16x2 green (parallel, LiquidCrystal)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A 16x2 character LCD (HD44780) with green text, wired the classic parallel way: RS, E and four data pins, as in Arduino's LiquidCrystal examples. Includes LiquidCrystal.h for sketches. Needs its contrast pin (V0) set, like the real one.

libraries.name: LED matrix 8x8 (MAX7219)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The common red 8x8 LED matrix module with a MAX7219 driver: 64 LEDs from 3 pins (DIN, CS, CLK). Includes LedControl.h for sketches.

libraries.name: Light and colour sensors
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A light-dependent resistor module (LDR), a BH1750 light meter (lux, I2C) and a TCS34725 colour sensor (I2C). They see the bench: the room light (the toolbar's Room button), anything held over them, and lit LEDs and screens. Includes BH1750.h and Adafruit_TCS34725.h.

libraries.name: Motion sensors
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Sensors that feel how they move and which way they face: a tilt switch, a compass (QMC5883L, as on the GY-271) an ADXL345 accelerometer and a PMW3901 optical flow sensor (it sees the floor slide past: how far it moved, for drones and rovers). They feel the real motion of whatever they're glued to: pick it up with the hand and tilt it. Also sketch libraries for the app's own MPU-6050 (Adafruit_MPU6050.h and MPU6050.h), and a self-balancing robot to build on.

libraries.name: Motor drivers and movers
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: More ways to drive and move things: the TB6612FNG (two small motors, efficient) and BTS7960 (one big motor, 43 A) drivers, a vibration motor that really shakes what it's on, a push-pull solenoid, and a linear actuator.

libraries.name: NeoPixel LEDs (WS2812B)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Addressable RGB LEDs (WS2812B, "NeoPixels"): a stick of 8, a strip of 30 and an 8x8 panel. One data wire sets every LED's colour; chain them DOUT to DIN. Includes Adafruit_NeoPixel.h.

libraries.name: Radio (nRF24L01)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The nRF24L01+ 2.4 GHz radio module (SPI): two boards send each other small messages (up to 32 bytes) with acknowledgements and retries, as the real chip does. Both need the same channel, data rate and address. Includes RF24.h.

libraries.name: OLED display (SSD1306)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The little I2C OLED screens (SSD1306): 128x64 and 128x32 pixels, white, blue or yellow-and-blue. Text, lines, shapes and pictures with Adafruit_SSD1306.h and Adafruit_GFX.h. The part speaks the real SSD1306 commands.

libraries.name: PS2 wireless controller
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The PS2-style wireless game pad that comes with most robot car kits: its receiver goes on the board (PS2X_lib.h), the pad's buttons and sticks drive the robot. Play it with a real game pad plugged into your PC, the keyboard (arrows, 1-4, Q/E, Enter), or the run panel.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: LoRa radio, CAN bus and RS485
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Talking further and tougher: a LoRa radio (SX1278, long range, slow; LoRa.h), a CAN bus module (MCP2515 + TJA1050, as in cars; mcp_can.h) and an RS485 transceiver (MAX485, long wires in noisy places, with Serial). Radios on the same frequency and settings hear each other; CAN and RS485 modules talk over their wires.

libraries.name: Relay module
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A 5 V relay on a module: a board's pin switches a separate circuit (a lamp, a motor, a pump) through its COM, NO and NC contacts. It clicks.

libraries.name: RFID reader (RC522) and tags
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The RC522 RFID reader (SPI) with MIFARE Classic tags: a white card and a blue key fob. Hold a tag up to the reader (drag it within a few cm of the coil) and the program reads its ID, and can read and write its 1 KB memory. Includes MFRC522.h.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: SD card module
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: A micro-SD card module (SPI) for keeping data: log readings to a file, read them back. The card holds its files while the run lasts (stop the run and it's a fresh card; its files are listed in the run panel). Includes SD.h.

libraries.name: More servos: 360, continuous, winch and smart
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Servos beyond 180 degrees. Continuous ones that spin round and round (FS90R, MG996R 360: the signal sets speed and direction), positional ones with 270 and 360 degrees of travel, a sail winch servo that turns three and a half turns, and two smart serial-bus servos that turn to any angle and report back (Feetech STS3215 with SCServo.h, Dynamixel XL430 with Dynamixel2Arduino.h).

libraries.name: Shift register (74HC595)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The 74HC595 on a little board: eight more outputs from three pins. shiftOut() the bits on DS and SHCP, then pulse STCP to show them on Q0-Q7. Comes with a light-chaser example on eight LEDs.

libraries.name: Stepper motors
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Two stepper motors with their drivers: the small 28BYJ-48 on a ULN2003 board (4 pins) and a NEMA 17 on an A4988 driver (STEP and DIR). They turn exactly as many steps as they're given, hold their position, and skip steps when overloaded or rushed. Includes Stepper.h and AccelStepper.h.

libraries.name: Colour TFTs, round and e-paper displays
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Full-colour SPI screens: the 1.8" ST7735 (128 x 160) and the 2.8" ILI9341 (240 x 320). Draw shapes, text and pictures with the Adafruit GFX functions. Includes Adafruit_ST7735.h, Adafruit_ILI9341.h, Adafruit_ST7789.h and Adafruit_GFX.h. Also a 240 x 240 ST7789, a round GC9A01 (1.28", for watch faces and gauges) and a 2.13" e-paper panel (Adafruit_EPD: it keeps its picture with the power off).

libraries.name: 4-digit display (TM1637)
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: The red 4-digit 7-segment display with a colon (a clock display) on a TM1637 chip: two wires, CLK and DIO. Includes TM1637Display.h. The part decodes the real TM1637 signals bit by bit.

libraries.name: Touch, force and weight
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Parts that feel what presses on them, from the real physics: a touch pad (TTP223), a force pad (FSR), a limit switch and a robot bumper, a slide potentiometer you push with the ball or drag, and a kitchen scale (load cell + HX711) that weighs what you put on it. Includes HX711.h.
can: have controls in the run panel

libraries.name: Soil, water, gas, flame, magnet and pulse sensors
libraries.author: Bench Workshop
libraries.description: Sensors for the world around a project: soil moisture (capacitive), water level, MQ-2 gas and smoke (with its warm-up), an IR flame sensor, a hall-effect magnet sensor and a pulse (heartbeat) sensor. What they sense is set in the run panel while it runs: how wet the soil is, how much gas, a finger on the pulse sensor.
can: have controls in the run panel
